summary: Creating an X developer account, app, and OAuth credentials is quick — but as of February 6, 2026, new developers get no free API tier. Every API call is pay-per-use, so the OAuth app works immediately while the API itself is unusable until billing is set up and credits are purchased.

decision.question: OAuth 1.0a or OAuth 2.0 with PKCE?

options.name: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE
pickWhen: You need fine-grained scopes or X API v2 user-context endpoints
options.tradeoff: X's recommended, actively supported method — requires implementing PKCE correctly.

options.name: OAuth 1.0a (3-legged)
pickWhen: You're integrating with an older library or tutorial built around it
You need direct account delegation without PKCE
options.tradeoff: Still supported, but considered the older method — new integrations should prefer OAuth 2.0.

decision.recommendation: Use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE unless you have a specific reason to use OAuth 1.0a — it's X's recommended method and required for v2 user-context endpoints.

difficultyReason: Creating the developer account and OAuth app is instant. But since February 6, 2026, new developers get no free API tier — every API call is pay-per-use, and no request succeeds until a payment method is added and credits are purchased. Free access exists only for 'Public Utility' apps approved case by case, not available on request.

time.setup: 10-20 min to create the account, app, and OAuth credentials
time.approvalWait: None to create the app and get API keys — there's no approval queue for pay-per-use access itself. But the app can't successfully call the API until billing is set up and credits are purchased.
time.notes: This setup time covers account/app creation only. Budget separate time to add billing before any API call will succeed — see accessCost below.

accessCost.pricingModel: Pay-per-use, credit-based. No subscription, no free tier for new developers as of Feb 6, 2026 — add a payment method, buy credits, and each API call deducts from the balance.
accessCost.rates: $0.005 per post read, $0.010 per user profile or DM read, $0.001 per owned-resource read, $0.015 per post created, $0.20 per post created containing a URL. New developers get a one-time $20 credit on adding a card, plus a match of up to $50 on first auto-recharge.
accessCost.freeTierLimits: No free tier for new developers. The only free-access path is the 'Public Utility' program — free scaled access for apps judged to serve the public good, approved case by case, not available by simply signing up. Even on paid pay-per-use, reads are capped at 3,000,000 posts/month before an Enterprise contract is required.

whenReviewIsNeeded.text: Free scaled API access (the 'Public Utility' program) is granted only case by case to apps judged to serve the public good — it is not a signup option.

requirements.text: An X account to sign in to the Developer Portal with.
A payment method and prepaid credits. The app can be created without one, but no API call will succeed until billing is set up.
A redirect/callback URL to register (up to 10 allowed per app); must be HTTPS and match exactly, including trailing slash, for production use.

steps.title: Start building: Create a developer account and app
steps.detail: Sign in to console.x.com with your X account, accept the Developer Agreement, click 'New App', and name it. Copy and store the generated API Key, API Secret, and Access Tokens immediately — they're shown once.

steps.title: Start building: Choose OAuth 1.0a or OAuth 2.0 with PKCE
steps.detail: See the decision above. For new integrations, configure OAuth 2.0 with PKCE under the app's authentication settings — it's required for X API v2 user-context endpoints.

steps.title: Start building: Register your redirect URI
steps.detail: Add the callback URL (up to 10 allowed) to the app's allowlist in the Developer Console. Must be HTTPS for production (http://127.0.0.1 is fine for local dev) and match exactly, including trailing slash.

steps.title: Start building: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL, redirect the user, handle the callback, and exchange the code for access tokens — using PKCE for OAuth 2.0 or the 3-legged flow for OAuth 1.0a.

steps.title: Go live: Add billing and buy credits
steps.detail: In the Developer Console, add a payment method and purchase credits. A successful OAuth flow does not mean the API is usable — every request fails until the account has a positive credit balance.

blockers.problem: API calls fail with no credits, even with valid OAuth tokens.
blockers.fix: Add a payment method and purchase credits in the Developer Console before making any API call — completing the OAuth flow successfully does not mean the API is usable.

blockers.problem: Old tutorials reference free/Basic tiers that no longer exist for new developers.
blockers.fix: As of Feb 6, 2026, new developer signups default to pay-per-use with no free tier; the Basic ($200/mo) and Pro ($5,000/mo) subscription tiers are closed to new signups (existing subscribers keep them or can opt into pay-per-use). Verify current pricing on docs.x.com directly rather than trusting an older guide.

agentCanDo: Exchange the authorization code for an access token (OAuth 2.0 PKCE or OAuth 1.0a 3-legged)
Refresh the access token when it expires
humanMustDo: Create the developer account and app in the X Developer Console
Set up billing and buy credits — no API call works without this
Apply separately for Public Utility free access if applicable — not guaranteed
openQuestions: Exact per-call rates may change; verify on the X developer portal before budgeting.
Whether the 3,000,000 post-reads/month cap before requiring an Enterprise contract has changed since this guide was last verified.
